defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal do
  @moduledoc """
  Client-facing portal domain: magic-link session tokens for clients
  (no password accounts), the client's view of upcoming visits with
  assigned-cleaner identity, service history with proof-of-work, and
  self-service reschedule/cancel enforcement against the account's
  cancellation policy.

  Every function here takes a `CleanerCrm.Clients.Client` directly
  rather than a `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` — a portal visitor is a
  client reached through a magic link, never a logged-in staff user.
  Internally, calls into `Scheduling`, `Quality`, `Billing`, and
  `Notifications` are scoped by deriving a `Scope` from the client's
  own `account_id`.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal.{CancellationPolicy, PortalSession, Tip}
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Magic-link sessions

  @doc """
  Issues a fresh portal session for `client`, returning the record
  with its plaintext `:token` set — the only time that token is ever
  available, so the caller (booking confirmation, "email me a link")
  must send or redirect with it immediately.
  """
  def create_portal_session(%Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    client
    |> PortalSession.build_changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Exchanges a magic-link token for the client id it grants access to.
  Touches the session's `last_used_at` on success. Fails closed with
  `{:error, :invalid}` for a token that doesn't match any session, or
  one that's expired — a client offered the same "your link is
  invalid or expired" outcome either way, never told which.
  """
  def access_portal(token) when is_binary(token) do
    case Repo.get_by(PortalSession, token_hash: PortalSession.hash_token(token)) do
      nil -> {:error, :invalid}
      %PortalSession{} = session -> exchange(session)
    end
  end

  defp exchange(%PortalSession{} = session) do
    if PortalSession.expired?(session) do
      {:error, :invalid}
    else
      {:ok, _touched} = session |> PortalSession.touch_changeset() |> Repo.update()
      {:ok, session.client_id}
    end
  end

  @doc "Loads a client by id — the portal session carries only the id, never the whole struct."
  def get_client!(client_id), do: Repo.get!(Client, client_id)

  ## Visits

  @doc """
  The client's upcoming (today or later, not cancelled) visits,
  soonest first, cleaner preloaded for name/photo display.
  """
  def list_upcoming_visits(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status in [:scheduled, :in_progress]))
    |> Enum.filter(&(Date.compare(&1.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :lt))
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.scheduled_date, &1.start_time})
  end

  @doc """
  The client's completed visits, most recent first — each one's
  checklist and before/after photos are read separately via
  `visit_checklist/1`.
  """
  def list_visit_history(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status == :completed))
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.scheduled_date, {:desc, Date})
  end

  @doc "A completed visit's checklist with items and photos preloaded, or `nil` if it has none."
  def visit_checklist(%Job{} = job) do
    Quality.get_checklist_for_job(system_scope(job.account_id), job)
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single visit for the portal's visit-detail page. Raises
  if `job_id` doesn't belong to `client` — the account-scoped lookup
  alone isn't enough, since other clients on the same account must
  never reach each other's visits by guessing an id.
  """
  def get_visit!(%Client{} = client, job_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(account_scope(client), job_id)

    case job.client_id do
      client_id when client_id == client.id -> job
      _other -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: Job
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Reschedules a visit to a new date/start time, preserving its
  original duration, agreed price, and assigned cleaner. Notifies the
  assigned cleaner (and, through their unacknowledged status, the
  office) the same way a staff-driven reschedule does. Refused with
  `{:error, :not_modifiable}` for a completed or already-cancelled
  visit, or `{:error, :slot_in_past}` for a date/time no longer ahead
  of `now` — mirrors `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_in_future?/2`,
  since without this a client could reschedule into a past date with
  zero validation. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes an
  override for tests.
  """
  def reschedule_visit(client, job, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def reschedule_visit(
        %Client{} = client,
        %Job{} = job,
        %{"date" => date_input, "start_time" => start_time_input},
        now
      ) do
    scope = account_scope(client)

    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job),
         {:ok, date} <- parse_date(date_input),
         {:ok, start_time} <- parse_time(start_time_input),
         :ok <- ensure_slot_in_future(date, start_time, now),
         {:ok, updated} <-
           Scheduling.update_job(scope, job, %{
             scheduled_date: date,
             start_time: start_time,
             end_time: shift_end_time(job, start_time)
           }) do
      notify_schedule_change(
        scope,
        updated,
        "Visit rescheduled by the client from #{schedule_label(job)} to #{schedule_label(updated)}"
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  The fee a client would be charged for cancelling `job` right now:
  the account's same-day fee if the visit is scheduled for today, its
  late fee if cancelling inside the notice window, otherwise zero.
  """
  def cancellation_fee_cents(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job) do
    policy = get_cancellation_policy(client.account_id)
    fee_for(policy, job)
  end

  defp fee_for(%CancellationPolicy{} = policy, %Job{} = job) do
    cond do
      Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) == :eq -> policy.same_day_fee_cents
      hours_until_visit(job) < policy.notice_window_hours -> policy.late_fee_cents
      true -> 0
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Cancels a visit, refusing with `{:error, :not_modifiable}` for one
  already completed or cancelled. Returns the fee charged alongside
  the updated visit — computed against the moment cancellation was
  requested, not looked up again afterward — and notifies the
  assigned cleaner of the cancellation.
  """
  def cancel_visit(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job) do
    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job) do
      scope = account_scope(client)
      fee_cents = cancellation_fee_cents(client, job)

      with {:ok, updated} <- Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job) do
        notify_schedule_change(scope, updated, "Visit cancelled by the client")
        {:ok, updated, fee_cents}
      end
    end
  end

  ## Cancellation policy

  @doc "The account's cancellation policy, defaulting to a fresh, unsaved (all-zero-fee) one."
  def get_cancellation_policy(account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(CancellationPolicy, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %CancellationPolicy{account_id: account_id}
      policy -> policy
    end
  end

  @doc "Sets (creating or updating) the account's cancellation policy."
  def set_cancellation_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    account_id
    |> get_cancellation_policy()
    |> CancellationPolicy.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc """
  A changeset for editing the account's cancellation policy — the
  owner settings form's own basis, same shape whether the account has
  a saved policy yet or is still on the unsaved, all-zero-fee default.
  """
  def change_cancellation_policy(%Scope{}, %CancellationPolicy{} = policy, attrs \\ %{}) do
    CancellationPolicy.changeset(policy, attrs)
  end

  ## Invoices and payment

  @doc "Every invoice for `client`'s own jobs, most recent first."
  def list_invoices(%Client{} = client) do
    Invoice
    |> join(:inner, [i], j in Job, on: j.id == i.job_id)
    |> where([i, j], j.client_id == ^client.id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Pays an invoice from the portal: submits the charge (per the
  payments-stripe ADR, this only moves the invoice to
  `:charge_pending` — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven), then
  optionally saves the card on file and records a tip against the
  visit's assigned cleaner.

  `attrs` (string-keyed, straight off the payment form): `"card_token"`
  (required), `"save_card"` (`"true"`/`"on"` to save), `"tip_cents"`
  (blank or omitted to skip the tip).
  """
  def pay_invoice(%Client{} = client, %Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    with {:ok, updated_invoice} <- Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, Map.get(attrs, "card_token")) do
      maybe_save_card(client, attrs)
      maybe_record_tip(updated_invoice, attrs)
      {:ok, updated_invoice}
    end
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(%Client{} = client, %{"save_card" => save_card})
       when save_card in ["true", "on"] do
    Clients.update_client(system_scope(client.account_id), client, %{card_on_file: true})
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(_client, _attrs), do: :ok

  defp maybe_record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    case parse_tip_cents(Map.get(attrs, "tip_cents")) do
      cents when is_integer(cents) and cents > 0 -> record_tip(invoice, cents)
      _no_tip -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, cents) do
    %Tip{
      account_id: invoice.account_id,
      invoice_id: invoice.id,
      cleaner_id: invoice.job.cleaner_id
    }
    |> Tip.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: cents,
      stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Cents a cleaner has been tipped through the portal within `period`
  (a `{start_date, end_date}` tuple, matching
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period/1`'s own shape) — read
  by `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent` to fold tips into a
  cleaner's pay-period total alongside their time-tracked earnings.
  """
  def tip_cents_for_cleaner(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        {start_date, end_date}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    Tip
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        t.inserted_at >= ^start_at and t.inserted_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> select([t], sum(t.amount_cents))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> Kernel.||(0)
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  defp account_scope(%Client{account_id: account_id}), do: system_scope(account_id)

  defp system_scope(account_id), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{status: status}) when status in [:completed, :cancelled],
    do: {:error, :not_modifiable}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{}), do: :ok

  defp ensure_slot_in_future(date, start_time, now) do
    if slot_in_future?(date, start_time, now), do: :ok, else: {:error, :slot_in_past}
  end

  # Mirrors `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_in_future?/2`'s own
  # date/time-vs-`now` comparison — today only counts if `start_time`
  # hasn't passed yet.
  defp slot_in_future?(date, start_time, now) do
    case Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) do
      :gt -> true
      :lt -> false
      :eq -> Time.compare(start_time, DateTime.to_time(now)) == :gt
    end
  end

  defp parse_date(%Date{} = date), do: {:ok, date}
  defp parse_date(string) when is_binary(string), do: Date.from_iso8601(string)

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _other -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when value in [nil, ""], do: nil

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when is_binary(value) do
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {cents, _rest} -> cents
      :error -> nil
    end
  end

  # Moves `start_time` in by the same amount the visit already runs,
  # clamping to end-of-day rather than wrapping past midnight into an
  # earlier clock time — mirrors
  # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`' own `default_end_time/1` safeguard.
  defp shift_end_time(%Job{} = job, %Time{} = start_time) do
    {start_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.start_time)
    {end_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.end_time)
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, end_seconds - start_seconds, :second)

    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  defp hours_until_visit(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}) do
    visit_at = DateTime.new!(date, time, "Etc/UTC")
    DateTime.diff(visit_at, DateTime.utc_now(), :hour)
  end

  defp notify_schedule_change(_scope, %Job{cleaner_id: nil}, _summary), do: :ok

  defp notify_schedule_change(scope, %Job{} = job, summary) do
    Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
      cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :schedule_change,
      channel: :push,
      status: :pending,
      change_summary: summary,
      pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      token: "portal_schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
    })
  end

  defp schedule_label(%Job{} = job),
    do:
      "#{job.scheduled_date} #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)}-#{format_time_12h(job.end_time)}"

  defp format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do
    {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour)
    minute = time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")
    "#{hour}:#{minute} #{period}"
  end

  defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal do
  @moduledoc """
  Client-facing portal domain: magic-link session tokens for clients
  (no password accounts), the client's view of upcoming visits with
  assigned-cleaner identity, service history with proof-of-work, and
  self-service reschedule/cancel enforcement against the account's
  cancellation policy.

  Every function here takes a `CleanerCrm.Clients.Client` directly
  rather than a `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` — a portal visitor is a
  client reached through a magic link, never a logged-in staff user.
  Internally, calls into `Scheduling`, `Quality`, `Billing`, and
  `Notifications` are scoped by deriving a `Scope` from the client's
  own `account_id`.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal.{CancellationPolicy, PortalSession, Tip}
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Magic-link sessions

  @doc """
  Issues a fresh portal session for `client`, returning the record
  with its plaintext `:token` set — the only time that token is ever
  available, so the caller (booking confirmation, "email me a link")
  must send or redirect with it immediately.
  """
  def create_portal_session(%Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    client
    |> PortalSession.build_changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Exchanges a magic-link token for the client id it grants access to.
  Touches the session's `last_used_at` on success. Fails closed with
  `{:error, :invalid}` for a token that doesn't match any session, or
  one that's expired — a client offered the same "your link is
  invalid or expired" outcome either way, never told which.
  """
  def access_portal(token) when is_binary(token) do
    case Repo.get_by(PortalSession, token_hash: PortalSession.hash_token(token)) do
      nil -> {:error, :invalid}
      %PortalSession{} = session -> exchange(session)
    end
  end

  defp exchange(%PortalSession{} = session) do
    if PortalSession.expired?(session) do
      {:error, :invalid}
    else
      {:ok, _touched} = session |> PortalSession.touch_changeset() |> Repo.update()
      {:ok, session.client_id}
    end
  end

  @doc "Loads a client by id — the portal session carries only the id, never the whole struct."
  def get_client!(client_id), do: Repo.get!(Client, client_id)

  ## Visits

  @doc """
  The client's upcoming (today or later, not cancelled) visits,
  soonest first, cleaner preloaded for name/photo display.
  """
  def list_upcoming_visits(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status in [:scheduled, :in_progress]))
    |> Enum.filter(&(Date.compare(&1.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :lt))
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.scheduled_date, &1.start_time})
  end

  @doc """
  The client's completed visits, most recent first — each one's
  checklist and before/after photos are read separately via
  `visit_checklist/1`.
  """
  def list_visit_history(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status == :completed))
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.scheduled_date, {:desc, Date})
  end

  @doc "A completed visit's checklist with items and photos preloaded, or `nil` if it has none."
  def visit_checklist(%Job{} = job) do
    Quality.get_checklist_for_job(system_scope(job.account_id), job)
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single visit for the portal's visit-detail page. Raises
  if `job_id` doesn't belong to `client` — the account-scoped lookup
  alone isn't enough, since other clients on the same account must
  never reach each other's visits by guessing an id.
  """
  def get_visit!(%Client{} = client, job_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(account_scope(client), job_id)

    case job.client_id do
      client_id when client_id == client.id -> job
      _other -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: Job
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Reschedules a visit to a new date/start time, preserving its
  original duration, agreed price, and assigned cleaner. Notifies the
  assigned cleaner (and, through their unacknowledged status, the
  office) the same way a staff-driven reschedule does. Refused with
  `{:error, :not_modifiable}` for a completed or already-cancelled
  visit, or `{:error, :slot_in_past}` for a date/time no longer ahead
  of `now` — mirrors `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_in_future?/2`,
  since without this a client could reschedule into a past date with
  zero validation. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes an
  override for tests.
  """
  def reschedule_visit(client, job, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def reschedule_visit(
        %Client{} = client,
        %Job{} = job,
        %{"date" => date_input, "start_time" => start_time_input},
        now
      ) do
    scope = account_scope(client)

    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job),
         {:ok, date} <- parse_date(date_input),
         {:ok, start_time} <- parse_time(start_time_input),
         :ok <- ensure_slot_in_future(date, start_time, now),
         {:ok, updated} <-
           Scheduling.update_job(scope, job, %{
             scheduled_date: date,
             start_time: start_time,
             end_time: shift_end_time(job, start_time)
           }) do
      notify_schedule_change(
        scope,
        updated,
        "Visit rescheduled by the client from #{schedule_label(job)} to #{schedule_label(updated)}"
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  The fee a client would be charged for cancelling `job` right now:
  the account's same-day fee if the visit is scheduled for today, its
  late fee if cancelling inside the notice window, otherwise zero.
  """
  def cancellation_fee_cents(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job) do
    policy = get_cancellation_policy(client.account_id)
    fee_for(policy, job)
  end

  defp fee_for(%CancellationPolicy{} = policy, %Job{} = job) do
    cond do
      Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) == :eq -> policy.same_day_fee_cents
      hours_until_visit(job) < policy.notice_window_hours -> policy.late_fee_cents
      true -> 0
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Cancels a visit, refusing with `{:error, :not_modifiable}` for one
  already completed or cancelled. Returns the fee charged alongside
  the updated visit — computed against the moment cancellation was
  requested, not looked up again afterward — and notifies the
  assigned cleaner of the cancellation.
  """
  def cancel_visit(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job) do
    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job) do
      scope = account_scope(client)
      fee_cents = cancellation_fee_cents(client, job)

      with {:ok, updated} <- Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job) do
        notify_schedule_change(scope, updated, "Visit cancelled by the client")
        {:ok, updated, fee_cents}
      end
    end
  end

  ## Cancellation policy

  @doc "The account's cancellation policy, defaulting to a fresh, unsaved (all-zero-fee) one."
  def get_cancellation_policy(account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(CancellationPolicy, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %CancellationPolicy{account_id: account_id}
      policy -> policy
    end
  end

  @doc "Sets (creating or updating) the account's cancellation policy."
  def set_cancellation_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    account_id
    |> get_cancellation_policy()
    |> CancellationPolicy.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc """
  A changeset for editing the account's cancellation policy — the
  owner settings form's own basis, same shape whether the account has
  a saved policy yet or is still on the unsaved, all-zero-fee default.
  """
  def change_cancellation_policy(%Scope{}, %CancellationPolicy{} = policy, attrs \\ %{}) do
    CancellationPolicy.changeset(policy, attrs)
  end

  ## Invoices and payment

  @doc "Every invoice for `client`'s own jobs, most recent first."
  def list_invoices(%Client{} = client) do
    Invoice
    |> join(:inner, [i], j in Job, on: j.id == i.job_id)
    |> where([i, j], j.client_id == ^client.id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Pays an invoice from the portal: submits the charge (per the
  payments-stripe ADR, this only moves the invoice to
  `:charge_pending` — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven), then
  optionally saves the card on file and records a tip against the
  visit's assigned cleaner.

  `attrs` (string-keyed, straight off the payment form): `"card_token"`
  (required), `"save_card"` (`"true"`/`"on"` to save), `"tip_cents"`
  (blank or omitted to skip the tip).
  """
  def pay_invoice(%Client{} = client, %Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    with {:ok, updated_invoice} <- Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, Map.get(attrs, "card_token")) do
      maybe_save_card(client, attrs)
      maybe_record_tip(updated_invoice, attrs)
      {:ok, updated_invoice}
    end
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(%Client{} = client, %{"save_card" => save_card})
       when save_card in ["true", "on"] do
    Clients.update_client(system_scope(client.account_id), client, %{card_on_file: true})
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(_client, _attrs), do: :ok

  defp maybe_record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    case parse_tip_cents(Map.get(attrs, "tip_cents")) do
      cents when is_integer(cents) and cents > 0 -> record_tip(invoice, cents)
      _no_tip -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, cents) do
    %Tip{
      account_id: invoice.account_id,
      invoice_id: invoice.id,
      cleaner_id: invoice.job.cleaner_id
    }
    |> Tip.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: cents,
      stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Cents a cleaner has been tipped through the portal within `period`
  (a `{start_date, end_date}` tuple, matching
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period/1`'s own shape) — read
  by `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent` to fold tips into a
  cleaner's pay-period total alongside their time-tracked earnings.
  """
  def tip_cents_for_cleaner(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        {start_date, end_date}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    Tip
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        t.inserted_at >= ^start_at and t.inserted_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> select([t], sum(t.amount_cents))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> Kernel.||(0)
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  defp account_scope(%Client{account_id: account_id}), do: system_scope(account_id)

  defp system_scope(account_id), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{status: status}) when status in [:completed, :cancelled],
    do: {:error, :not_modifiable}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{}), do: :ok

  defp ensure_slot_in_future(date, start_time, now) do
    if slot_in_future?(date, start_time, now), do: :ok, else: {:error, :slot_in_past}
  end

  # Mirrors `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_in_future?/2`'s own
  # date/time-vs-`now` comparison — today only counts if `start_time`
  # hasn't passed yet.
  defp slot_in_future?(date, start_time, now) do
    case Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) do
      :gt -> true
      :lt -> false
      :eq -> Time.compare(start_time, DateTime.to_time(now)) == :gt
    end
  end

  defp parse_date(%Date{} = date), do: {:ok, date}
  defp parse_date(string) when is_binary(string), do: Date.from_iso8601(string)

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _other -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when value in [nil, ""], do: nil

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when is_binary(value) do
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {cents, _rest} -> cents
      :error -> nil
    end
  end

  # Moves `start_time` in by the same amount the visit already runs,
  # clamping to end-of-day rather than wrapping past midnight into an
  # earlier clock time — mirrors
  # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`' own `default_end_time/1` safeguard.
  defp shift_end_time(%Job{} = job, %Time{} = start_time) do
    {start_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.start_time)
    {end_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.end_time)
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, end_seconds - start_seconds, :second)

    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  defp hours_until_visit(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}) do
    visit_at = DateTime.new!(date, time, "Etc/UTC")
    DateTime.diff(visit_at, DateTime.utc_now(), :hour)
  end

  defp notify_schedule_change(_scope, %Job{cleaner_id: nil}, _summary), do: :ok

  defp notify_schedule_change(scope, %Job{} = job, summary) do
    Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
      cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :schedule_change,
      channel: :push,
      status: :pending,
      change_summary: summary,
      pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      token: "portal_schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
    })
  end

  defp schedule_label(%Job{} = job),
    do:
      "#{job.scheduled_date} #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)}-#{format_time_12h(job.end_time)}"

  defp format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do
    {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour)
    minute = time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")
    "#{hour}:#{minute} #{period}"
  end

  defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController do
  @moduledoc """
  The magic-link entry point into the client portal: `GET
  /portal/access/:token` exchanges a token (mailed to the client, or
  handed out at booking) for a portal session — no password
  required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Portal`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def access(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Portal.access_portal(token) do
      {:ok, client_id} ->
        conn
        |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client_id)
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/portal")

      {:error, :invalid} ->
        render(conn, :invalid)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth do
  @moduledoc """
  Gates the client portal's LiveViews behind a magic-link session —
  no user login. Reads the client id `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController`
  wrote to the session's `:portal_client_id` key after a valid
  `/portal/access/:token` exchange, mirroring how
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth` reads `:user_token` for staff auth.

  ## Usage

      live_session :portal,
        on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
        live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def on_mount(:require_client, _params, session, socket) do
    case session["portal_client_id"] do
      nil ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "Please use your portal link to sign in.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/")

        {:halt, socket}

      client_id ->
        {:cont,
         Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :client, fn -> Portal.get_client!(client_id) end)}
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}

  # Idempotent against a redelivered webhook — Stripe (and its Test
  # stand-in) offers no stronger delivery guarantee than at-least-once.
  defp convert_lead(%Lead{status: :converted} = lead), do: {:ok, lead}

  defp convert_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    scope = scope_for(lead)

    with {:ok, {updated, client}} <-
           Repo.transact(fn ->
             with {:ok, client} <- Clients.create_client(scope, client_attrs(lead)),
                  {:ok, property} <- Clients.create_property(scope, property_attrs(client)),
                  {:ok, visit_ids} <- schedule_visit(scope, lead, property),
                  {:ok, updated} <- finalize_conversion(lead, client, property, visit_ids) do
               {:ok, {updated, client}}
             end
           end) do
      issue_portal_access(updated, client)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp client_attrs(%Lead{} = lead) do
    %{
      name: lead.client_name,
      email: lead.client_email,
      phone: lead.client_phone,
      card_on_file: true
    }
  end

  # No property inputs exist anywhere in the public funnel (story 848's
  # form only ever asks for what prices the job) — the office fills
  # the real address in from the client record afterward. Named after
  # the client rather than a generic placeholder so the schedule board
  # (which shows a job's property, never its client, on the card) still
  # identifies whose visit this is until that happens.
  defp property_attrs(%Client{} = client) do
    %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "#{client.name} — address to be confirmed"}
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{frequency: :one_time} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             scheduled_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents,
             status: :scheduled
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: job.id, recurring_plan_id: nil}}
    end
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} <-
           Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             recurrence: lead.frequency,
             start_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             occurrence_count: @default_occurrence_count,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: nil, recurring_plan_id: plan.id}}
    end
  end

  defp finalize_conversion(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client, property, visit_ids) do
    lead
    |> Lead.changeset(
      Map.merge(%{status: :converted, client_id: client.id, property_id: property.id}, visit_ids)
    )
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp issue_portal_access(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client) do
    with {:ok, session} <- Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{}) do
      Notifier.deliver_confirmation(lead, portal_url(session))
    end
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp portal_url(session), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/portal/access/#{session.token}"

  defp scope_for(%Lead{account_id: account_id}), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          email: String.t() | nil,
          phone: String.t() | nil,
          preferred_channel: :email | :sms,
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false
    field :email, :string
    field :phone, :string
    field :preferred_channel, Ecto.Enum, values: [:email, :sms], default: :email

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file, :email, :phone, :preferred_channel])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Integrations.OAuthStateStore do
  use GenServer

  @table :oauth_state_store
  @ttl_seconds 300

  def start_link(_opts), do: GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, nil, name: __MODULE__)

  def store(state, session_params) when is_binary(state) do
    :ets.insert(@table, {state, session_params, System.system_time(:second)})
    :ok
  end

  def fetch(state) when is_binary(state) do
    case :ets.lookup(@table, state) do
      [{^state, session_params, ts}] ->
        :ets.delete(@table, state)

        if System.system_time(:second) - ts <= @ttl_seconds,
          do: {:ok, session_params},
          else: :error

      [] ->
        :error
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def init(_) do
    :ets.new(@table, [:named_table, :public, read_concurrency: true])
    schedule_cleanup()
    {:ok, %{}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info(:cleanup, state) do
    cutoff = System.system_time(:second) - @ttl_seconds
    :ets.select_delete(@table, [{{:_, :_, :"$1"}, [{:<, :"$1", cutoff}], [true]}])
    schedule_cleanup()
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  defp schedule_cleanup, do: Process.send_after(self(), :cleanup, 60_000)
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSession do
  @moduledoc """
  A magic-link access token that lets a client into their portal with
  no password account.

  The plaintext token is only ever held in memory — in the `:token`
  virtual field, right after `build_changeset/2` creates it — to be
  mailed or handed to the client; only its SHA-256 hash is persisted.
  This mirrors `CleanerCrm.Users.UserToken`'s own magic-link scheme, so
  read access to the database alone can never reconstruct a working
  token.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @hash_algorithm :sha256
  @rand_size 32
  @default_validity_in_days 7

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          token: String.t() | nil,
          token_hash: binary() | nil,
          expires_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          last_used_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "portal_sessions" do
    field :token, :string, virtual: true
    field :token_hash, :binary
    field :expires_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :last_used_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a fresh session for `client`: a random plaintext token (held
  only in the returned changeset's `:token` virtual field, for the
  caller to mail or hand back) and its hash, expiring
  #{@default_validity_in_days} days out unless `attrs` gives its own
  `:expires_at`.
  """
  def build_changeset(%{id: client_id, account_id: account_id}, attrs) do
    token = generate_token()

    %__MODULE__{account_id: account_id, client_id: client_id}
    |> cast(attrs, [:expires_at, :last_used_at])
    |> put_change(:token, token)
    |> put_change(:token_hash, hash_token(token))
    |> put_default_expiry()
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :client_id, :token_hash, :expires_at])
  end

  @doc "Marks the session used just now."
  def touch_changeset(%__MODULE__{} = session) do
    change(session, last_used_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  @doc "Hashes a plaintext token the same way `build_changeset/2` does, for lookup by token."
  def hash_token(token) when is_binary(token), do: :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, token)

  @doc "True once `expires_at` has passed."
  def expired?(%__MODULE__{expires_at: expires_at}),
    do: DateTime.compare(expires_at, DateTime.utc_now()) == :lt

  defp put_default_expiry(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :expires_at) do
      nil ->
        put_change(
          changeset,
          :expires_at,
          DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), @default_validity_in_days, :day)
        )

      _expires_at ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_token,
    do: @rand_size |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Application do
  # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Application.html
  # for more information on OTP Applications
  @moduledoc false

  use Application

  @impl true
  def start(_type, _args) do
    children = [
      CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry,
      CleanerCrm.Repo,
      {DNSCluster, query: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query) || :ignore},
      {Phoenix.PubSub, name: CleanerCrm.PubSub},
      CleanerCrm.Vault,
      CleanerCrm.Integrations.OAuthStateStore,
      {Oban, Application.fetch_env!(:cleaner_crm, Oban)},
      # Start a worker by calling: CleanerCrm.Worker.start_link(arg)
      # {CleanerCrm.Worker, arg},
      # Start to serve requests, typically the last entry
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint
    ]

    # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Supervisor.html
    # for other strategies and supported options
    opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: CleanerCrm.Supervisor]
    Supervisor.start_link(children, opts)
  end

  # Tell Phoenix to update the endpoint configuration
  # whenever the application is updated.
  @impl true
  def config_change(changed, _new, removed) do
    CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.config_change(changed, removed)
    :ok
  end
end

  those modules here.

defmodule CleanerCrm.PortalTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, account: account, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "create_portal_session/2 and access_portal/1" do
    test "a fresh token grants access to the client that issued it", %{client: client} do
      {:ok, session} = Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{})

      assert {:ok, client_id} = Portal.access_portal(session.token)
      assert client_id == client.id
    end
  end

  describe "access_portal/1 failure paths" do
    test "an expired session is refused", %{client: client} do
      {:ok, session} =
        Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{
          expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)
        })

      assert {:error, :invalid} = Portal.access_portal(session.token)
    end

    test "an unknown token is refused" do
      assert {:error, :invalid} = Portal.access_portal("not-a-real-token")
    end
  end

  describe "list_upcoming_visits/1 and list_visit_history/1" do
    test "upcoming visits excludes completed and cancelled jobs", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      upcoming = job_fixture(scope, client, %{})
      completed = job_fixture(scope, client, %{status: :completed})
      {:ok, cancelled} = Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job_fixture(scope, client, %{}))

      visits = Portal.list_upcoming_visits(client)

      assert Enum.map(visits, & &1.id) == [upcoming.id]
      refute Enum.any?(visits, &(&1.id == completed.id))
      refute Enum.any?(visits, &(&1.id == cancelled.id))
    end

    test "visit history only includes completed jobs", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job_fixture(scope, client, %{})
      completed = job_fixture(scope, client, %{status: :completed})

  import other functionality to make it easier

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.HomeTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp portal_conn(client) do
    build_conn()
    |> init_test_session(%{})
    |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  test "shows an upcoming visit's assigned cleaner and a completed visit's proof-of-work" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    cleaner = CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

    upcoming =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })
      |> then(fn {:ok, job} -> job end)

    {:ok, completed} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        status: :completed
      })

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      Quality.complete_checklist(scope, completed, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before.jpg",
          after_photo: "after.jpg"
        }
      ])

    {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal")

    assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='upcoming-visits']")
    assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='visit-#{upcoming.id}']", cleaner.name)

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='service-history'] [data-test='visit-#{completed.id}']",
             "Kitchen counters wiped down"
           )

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='visit-#{completed.id}'] [data-test='before-photo']"
           )
  end

  test "an unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder instead of a cleaner" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal")

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='visit-#{job.id}'] [data-test='cleaner-not-assigned']"
           )
  end

  test "redirects home when there is no portal session" do
    assert {:error, {:redirect, %{to: "/"}}} = live(build_conn(), ~p"/portal")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.UserNotifier do
  import Swoosh.Email

  alias CleanerCrm.Mailer
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  # Delivers the email using the application mailer.
  defp deliver(recipient, subject, body) do
    email =
      new()
      |> to(recipient)
      |> from(Application.fetch_env!(:cleaner_crm, :mailer_from))
      |> subject(subject)
      |> text_body(body)

    with {:ok, _metadata} <- Mailer.deliver(email) do

def create_portal_session(%Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    client
    |> PortalSession.build_changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Handles a "request a login link" submission from
  `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.RequestLink`: mails a fresh magic link to
  every client, across every account, whose address matches `email` —
  the same client can be a customer of more than one cleaning
  company, and each relationship gets its own link to its own
  account's portal.

  Always returns `:ok`, whether or not `email` matches anyone, so the
  caller can show one generic "check your email" message without ever
  revealing which addresses belong to real clients. Matches skipped
  by the cooldown (see `@link_request_cooldown_seconds`) are silently
  treated the same as a match with nothing new to send.
  """
  def request_login_link(email) when is_binary(email) do
    email
    |> String.trim()
    |> clients_by_email()
    |> Enum.reject(&recently_sent_link?/1)
    |> Enum.each(&issue_and_deliver_link/1)

    :ok
  end

  defp clients_by_email(""), do: []

  defp clients_by_email(email) do
    Repo.all(from(c in Client, where: c.email == ^email))
  end

  defp recently_sent_link?(%Client{id: client_id}) do
    cutoff = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -@link_request_cooldown_seconds, :second)

    Repo.exists?(
      from(s in PortalSession, where: s.client_id == ^client_id and s.inserted_at >= ^cutoff)
    )
  end

  defp issue_and_deliver_link(%Client{} = client) do
    with {:ok, session} <- create_portal_session(client, %{}) do
      Notifier.deliver_login_link(client, portal_url(session))
    end
  end

""" import Swoosh.Email alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client alias CleanerCrm.Mailer def deliver_login_link(%Client{email: email} = client, portal_url) when is_binary(email) and is_binary(portal_url) do message = new() |> to(email) |> from(Application.fetch_env!(:cleaner_crm, :mailer_from)) |> subject("Your client portal link") |> html_body("""

Hi#{name_suffix(client)},

Here's the link you asked for: open your client portal.

If you didn't request this, you can safely ignore this email.

""") |> text_body(""" Hi#{name_suffix(client)}, Here's the link you asked for — open your client portal: #{portal_url} If you didn't request this, you can safely ignore this email. """) Mailer.deliver(message) end defp name_suffix(%Client{name: name}) when is_binary(name) and name != "", do: ", #{name}" defp name_suffix(_client), do: "" end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth do
  @moduledoc """
  Gates the client portal's LiveViews behind a magic-link session —
  no user login. Reads the client id `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController`
  wrote to the session's `:portal_client_id` key after a valid
  `/portal/access/:token` exchange, mirroring how
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth` reads `:user_token` for staff auth.

  ## Usage

      live_session :portal,
        on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
        live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def on_mount(:require_client, _params, session, socket) do
    case session["portal_client_id"] do
      nil ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "Please use your portal link to sign in.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/")

        {:halt, socket}

      client_id ->
        {:cont,
         Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :client, fn -> Portal.get_client!(client_id) end)}
    end
  end
end

  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index

    # "I lost/never got my link" — its own `live_session` (not the

    # mirrors the other public live routes above so `current_scope`
    # still mounts for the root layout.
    live_session :portal_request_link,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/portal/request-link", PortalLive.RequestLink, :new
    end
  end

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp portal_conn(client) do
    build_conn()
    |> init_test_session(%{})
    |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  test "shows an upcoming visit's assigned cleaner and a completed visit's proof-of-work" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    cleaner = CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

    upcoming =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],

      })

    {:ok, completed} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        status: :completed
      })

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      Quality.complete_checklist(scope, completed, [

          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before.jpg",

        }
      ])

    {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal")

    assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='upcoming-visits']")
    assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='visit-#{upcoming.id}']", cleaner.name)

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='service-history'] [data-test='visit-#{completed.id}']",
             "Kitchen counters wiped down"
           )

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='visit-#{completed.id}'] [data-test='before-photo']"
           )
  end

  test "an unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder instead of a cleaner" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal")

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='visit-#{job.id}'] [data-test='cleaner-not-assigned']"
           )
  end

  test "redirects home when there is no portal session" do
    assert {:error, {:redirect, %{to: "/"}}} = live(build_conn(), ~p"/portal")
  end
end

2	  @moduledoc ~S"""
3	  This module contains a set of assertions functions that you can import in your
4	  test cases.
5	
6	  It is meant to be used with the
7	  [Swoosh.Adapters.Test](Swoosh.Adapters.Test.html) module.
8	
9	  **Note**: `Swoosh.TestAssertions` works for unit tests and basic integration tests
10	  when using `Swoosh.Adapters.Test`.
11	
12	  For feature/E2E tests, use `Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox` instead.  The sandbox adapter
13	  supports per-test process ownership and explicit allows, so `assert_email_sent`
14	  works even when the delivering process (e.g. a Phoenix endpoint or LiveView) has
15	  no `$callers` ancestry back to the test process.  See
16	  `Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox` for setup instructions.
17	
18	  Alternatively, you can use `Swoosh.Adapters.Local` and check the local adapter
19	  mailbox or navigate to the preview URL with your E2E tool.
20	  """
21	
22	  import ExUnit.Assertions
23	
24	  alias Swoosh.Email
25	  alias Swoosh.Email.Recipient
26	
27	  @type email_assertion :: Email.t() | Keyword.t() | (Email.t() -> boolean())
28	
29	  @doc """
30	  Sets Swoosh test adapter to global mode.
31	
32	  In global mode, emails are consumed by the current test process,
33	  doesn't matter which process sent it.
34	
35	  An ExUnit case where tests use Swoosh in global mode cannot be `async: true`.
36	
37	  ## Examples
38	
39	      defmodule MyTest do
40	        use ExUnit.Case, async: false
41	
42	        import Swoosh.Email
43	        import Swoosh.TestAssertions
44	
45	        setup :set_swoosh_global
46	
47	        test "it sends email" do
48	          # ...
49	          assert_email_sent(subject: "Hi Avengers!")
50	        end
51	      end
52	  """
53	  def set_swoosh_global(context \\ %{}) do
54	    if Map.get(context, :async) do
55	      raise "Swoosh cannot be set to global mode when the ExUnit case is async. " <>
56	              "If you want to use Swoosh in global mode, remove \"async: true\" when using ExUnit.Case"
57	    else
58	      Application.put_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process, self())
59	
60	      ExUnit.Callbacks.on_exit(fn ->
61	        Application.delete_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process)
62	      end)
63	
64	      :ok
65	    end
66	  end

68	  @doc ~S"""
69	  Asserts any email was sent.
70	  """
71	  @spec assert_email_sent() :: tuple | no_return
72	  def assert_email_sent do
73	    assert_received {:email, _}
74	  end
75

77	          :ok | tuple | no_return
78

81

83	  or an anonymous function that returns a boolean.
84	
85	  ## Examples

defmodule Swoosh.TestAssertions do
  @moduledoc ~S"""
  This module contains a set of assertions functions that you can import in your
  test cases.

  It is meant to be used with the
  [Swoosh.Adapters.Test](Swoosh.Adapters.Test.html) module.

  **Note**: `Swoosh.TestAssertions` works for unit tests and basic integration tests
  when using `Swoosh.Adapters.Test`.

  For feature/E2E tests, use `Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox` instead.  The sandbox adapter
  supports per-test process ownership and explicit allows, so `assert_email_sent`
  works even when the delivering process (e.g. a Phoenix endpoint or LiveView) has
  no `$callers` ancestry back to the test process.  See
  `Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox` for setup instructions.

  Alternatively, you can use `Swoosh.Adapters.Local` and check the local adapter
  mailbox or navigate to the preview URL with your E2E tool.
  """

  import ExUnit.Assertions

  alias Swoosh.Email
  alias Swoosh.Email.Recipient

  @type email_assertion :: Email.t() | Keyword.t() | (Email.t() -> boolean())

  @doc """
  Sets Swoosh test adapter to global mode.

  In global mode, emails are consumed by the current test process,
  doesn't matter which process sent it.

  An ExUnit case where tests use Swoosh in global mode cannot be `async: true`.

  ## Examples

      defmodule MyTest do
        use ExUnit.Case, async: false

        import Swoosh.Email
        import Swoosh.TestAssertions

        setup :set_swoosh_global

        test "it sends email" do
          # ...
          assert_email_sent(subject: "Hi Avengers!")
        end
      end
  """
  def set_swoosh_global(context \\ %{}) do
    if Map.get(context, :async) do
      raise "Swoosh cannot be set to global mode when the ExUnit case is async. " <>
              "If you want to use Swoosh in global mode, remove \"async: true\" when using ExUnit.Case"
    else
      Application.put_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process, self())

      ExUnit.Callbacks.on_exit(fn ->
        Application.delete_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process)
      end)

      :ok
    end
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts any email was sent.
  """
  @spec assert_email_sent() :: tuple | no_return
  def assert_email_sent do
    assert_received {:email, _}
  end

  @spec assert_email_sent(email_assertion()) ::
          :ok | tuple | no_return

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts `email` was sent.

  You can pass a keyword list to match on specific params
  or an anonymous function that returns a boolean.

  ## Examples

      iex> alias Swoosh.Email
      iex> import Swoosh.TestAssertions

      iex> email = Email.new(subject: "Hello, Avengers!")
      iex> Swoosh.Adapters.Test.deliver(email, [])

      # assert a specific email was sent
      iex> assert_email_sent(email)

      # assert an email with specific field(s) was sent
      iex> assert_email_sent(subject: "Hello, Avengers!")

      # assert an email that satisfies a condition
      iex> assert_email_sent(fn email ->
      ...>   assert length(email.to) == 2
      ...> end)
  """
  def assert_email_sent(%Email{} = email) do
    assert_received {:email, ^email}
  end

  def assert_email_sent(params) when is_list(params) do
    assert_received {:email, email}
    Enum.each(params, &assert_equal(email, &1))
  end

  def assert_email_sent(fun) when is_function(fun, 1) do
    assert_received {:email, email}
    assert fun.(email)
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts multiple emails were sent.

  You can pass a list of maps to match on specific params per email

  ## Examples

      iex> alias Swoosh.Email
      iex> import Swoosh.TestAssertions

      iex> emails = Enum.map(1..2, fn n -> Email.new(subject: "Hello, Avengers #{n}!") end)
      iex> Swoosh.Adapters.Test.deliver_many(emails, [])

      # assert a specific email was sent
      iex> assert_emails_sent(emails)

      # assert the list of emails with specific field(s) that were sent
      iex> assert_emails_sent([
        %{subject: "Hello, Avengers 1!"},
        %{subject: "Hello, Avengers 2!"},
      ])
  """
  @spec assert_emails_sent() :: tuple | no_return
  def assert_emails_sent do
    assert_receive {:emails, _}
  end

  @spec assert_emails_sent([email_assertion()]) ::
          :ok | tuple | no_return
  def assert_emails_sent([%Swoosh.Email{} | _] = emails) do
    assert_received {:emails, ^emails}
  end

  def assert_emails_sent([%{} | _] = params_map_list) do
    assert_received {:emails, emails}

    assert length(emails) == length(params_map_list)

    emails
    |> Enum.zip(params_map_list)
    |> Enum.each(fn {email, params_map} ->
      Enum.each(params_map, &assert_equal(email, &1))
    end)
  end

  defp assert_equal(email, {:subject, %Regex{} = value}),
    do: assert(email.subject =~ value)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:subject, value}),
    do: assert(email.subject == value)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:from, value}),
    do: assert(email.from == Recipient.format(value))

  defp assert_equal(email, {:reply_to, value}),
    do: assert(email.reply_to == Recipient.format(value))

  defp assert_equal(email, {:to, value}) when is_list(value),
    do: assert(email.to == Enum.map(value, &Recipient.format/1))

  defp assert_equal(email, {:to, value}),
    do: assert(Recipient.format(value) in email.to)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:cc, value}) when is_list(value),
    do: assert(email.cc == Enum.map(value, &Recipient.format/1))

  defp assert_equal(email, {:cc, value}),
    do: assert(Recipient.format(value) in email.cc)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:bcc, value}) when is_list(value),
    do: assert(email.bcc == Enum.map(value, &Recipient.format/1))

  defp assert_equal(email, {:bcc, value}),
    do: assert(Recipient.format(value) in email.bcc)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:text_body, %Regex{} = value}),
    do: assert(email.text_body =~ value)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:text_body, value}),
    do: assert(email.text_body == value)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:html_body, %Regex{} = value}),
    do: assert(email.html_body =~ value)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:html_body, value}),
    do: assert(email.html_body == value)

  defp assert_equal(email, {:headers, value}),
    do: assert(email.headers == value)

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts no emails were sent.
  """
  defmacro refute_email_sent() do
    quote do
      refute_received {:email, _}
    end
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Refutes any email was sent via `deliver_many`.
  """
  defmacro refute_emails_sent() do
    quote do
      refute_received {:emails, _}
    end
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts email with `attributes` was not sent.

  Performs pattern matching using the given pattern, equivalent to `pattern = email`.

  When a list of attributes is given, they will be converted to a pattern.

  It converts list fields (`:to`, `:cc`, `:bcc`) to a single element list if a single value is
  given (`to: "email@example.com"` => `to: ["email@example.com"]`).

  After conversion, performs pattern matching using a map of email attributes, similar to
  `%{attributes...} = email`.
  """
  defmacro refute_email_sent(attributes) when is_list(attributes) do
    quote do
      refute_email_sent(%{unquote_splicing(Enum.map(attributes, &email_pattern/1))})
    end
  end

  defmacro refute_email_sent(pattern) do
    quote do
      refute_received {:email, unquote(pattern)}
    end
  end

  defp email_pattern({key, value}) when key in [:from, :reply_to] do
    {key, Recipient.format(value)}
  end

  defp email_pattern({key, value}) when key in [:to, :cc, :bcc] do
    {key, value |> List.wrap() |> Enum.map(&Recipient.format/1)}
  end

  defp email_pattern({key, value}) do
    {key, value}
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts no emails were sent.
  """
  @spec assert_no_email_sent() :: false | no_return
  def assert_no_email_sent() do
    refute_email_sent()
    refute_emails_sent()
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Asserts `email` was not sent.

  Performs exact matching of the email struct.
  """
  @spec assert_email_not_sent(Email.t()) :: false | no_return
  def assert_email_not_sent(%Email{} = email) do
    refute_email_sent(^email)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.RequestLinkTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  test "an existing client's email creates a session and shows the generic message" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{email: "morgan@example.com"})

    {:ok, request_link_live, _html} = live(build_conn(), ~p"/portal/request-link")

    request_link_live
    |> form("#request_link_form", request_link: %{email: "morgan@example.com"})
    |> render_submit()

    assert_redirected(request_link_live, ~p"/portal/request-link")
    assert_email_sent(to: "morgan@example.com")
    assert Portal.get_client!(client.id)
  end

  test "an unknown email shows the same generic message and sends nothing" do
    {:ok, request_link_live, _html} = live(build_conn(), ~p"/portal/request-link")

    request_link_live
    |> form("#request_link_form", request_link: %{email: "nobody@example.com"})
    |> render_submit()

    assert_redirected(request_link_live, ~p"/portal/request-link")
    assert_no_email_sent()
  end

  test "PortalAuth redirects a sessionless /portal visit here" do
    assert {:error, {:redirect, %{to: "/portal/request-link"}}} = live(build_conn(), ~p"/portal")
  end
end

def assert_redirected(view, to) do
    assert_redirect(view, to, 0)
  end

  defp assert_navigation(view, kind, to, timeout) do
    %{proxy: {ref, topic, _}, endpoint: endpoint} = view

    receive do
      {^ref, {^kind, ^topic, %{to: new_to} = opts}} when new_to == to or to == nil ->
        {new_to, Phoenix.LiveView.Utils.verify_flash(endpoint, opts[:flash])}
    after
      timeout ->
        message =
          if to do
            "expected #{inspect(view.module)} to #{kind} to #{inspect(to)}, "
          else
            "expected #{inspect(view.module)} to #{kind}, "
          end

        case flush_navigation(ref, topic, nil) do
          {new_kind, new_to} when new_to != to ->
            raise ArgumentError, message <> "but got a #{new_kind} to #{inspect(new_to)}"

          _ ->
            raise ArgumentError, message <> "but got none"
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Refutes a redirect to a given path was performed.

  It returns :ok if the specified redirect isn't already in the mailbox.

  If no path is specified, refutes any redirection on the given view.

  ## Examples

content.content:
mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

## Configuration

You can configure spex behavior in your config files:

    config :sexy_spex,
      manual_mode: false,
      step_delay: 0

Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all
blocks.

## Important: Test Environment Setup

To ensure spex runs in the test environment with proper module compilation, add
this to your project's mix.exs:

    def project do
      [
        # ... other config
        preferred_cli_env: [
          spex: :test
        ]
      ]
    end

This ensures that `mix spex` always runs in the test environment and compiles
modules with test-specific code paths (e.g., test/support directories).

content.text:
Sent the completion summary to team-lead. Here's the final state of the work:

**Built:** GET `/portal/request-link` — a public "get portal access" page for clients who lost or never got their magic link.

- `lib/cleaner_crm/portal.ex` — added `request_login_link/1` (additive, exact-match by email across all accounts, one link per matching client, 60-second cooldown per client backed by `PortalSession.inserted_at`, always returns `:ok` with no account-enumeration signal)
- `lib/cleaner_crm/portal/notifier.ex` (new) — `deliver_login_link/2`, styled like `Booking.Notifier`
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/portal_live/request_link.ex` (new) — the LiveView, single email field, `variant={:portal}` layout
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/portal_auth.ex` — no-session `/portal` visits now redirect to `/portal/request-link` instead of dead-ending at `/`
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/controllers/portal_html/invalid.html.heex` — "Request a new link" now points at the new page instead of a mailto link
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/router.ex` — one additive public `live_session` in the existing portal scope
- Tests: 4 new cases in `portal_test.exs`, 3 new cases in `request_link_test.exs`, one stale assertion fixed in `home_test.exs`

Verified clean: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, full `mix test` (273 tests, 0 failures), the required spex suites 850/851/852 (21 tests, 0 failures), and `mix format`. I left the concurrent booking/accounts/rate_card changes from the other in-progress task untouched.

**This needs a release rebuild** before it's live.
